polities: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve
pacing: Playback slows only while a polity delivered by a route on this map gains, or first takes, at least 100 cells (0.1 degree). Measured in cells, never screen pixels, so the pace never depends on the view.

Southern Song.html: THE SOURCE'S NAME FOR THIS GROUND IS WRONG, AND THIS MAP DRAWS IT AS THE SOURCE DOES. Cliopatria v0.2.0 ends its Northern Song in 1027 and names the same ground Southern Song from 1028. The Southern Song is conventionally dated from 1127, after the Jurchen Jin took Kaifeng; the name refers to that loss of the north. The source's own records disagree with its label: its three Southern Song shapes for 1028–1138 carry no Seshat polity ID and keep the Northern Song's extent (the 1028 shape is identical to its last Northern Song shape; the later two differ by under 2%), reaching about 39°N and containing Kaifeng, while the Seshat ID for the Southern Song (cn_southern_song_dyn) first appears on its 1139 shape, which stops south of 35°N and no longer contains Kaifeng. Nothing happened to the Song in 1028: the change of name and colour here is the source's, not history's. It is left as the source has it, because this map does not silently correct its sources.

method:
Input: the shipped act files (data/acts: Cliopatria v0.2.0, simplified 0.25 deg, 2 dp) for this act and the one
before it (for predecessor shapes), and the source geojson only for MemberOf (the composite a polity belongs to).
Output: data/borders/act_<from>_<to>.json (header) and .bin (grid and timed changes).

GRID. 0.1-degree cells over the act's extent. A cell's state is the SET of real (leaf) polities drawing it at that
moment. Composite "(...)" records are not drawn (C8); they name the occupier in the tooltip.

TIME. A Cliopatria record is a dated shape, valid from its first year to the end of its last. A spread is the change
from one record of a polity to its next. It starts at the new record's first year and is complete by the middle of
that record's span, so the map never shows ground before the source dates it, and every dated shape is reached
inside its own window.
 - GAINED cells arrive in order of distance measured through the new shape (8-neighbour shortest path; ground outside
   the shape costs 4x, so colour flows along coasts rather than jumping water), from the previous shape, from a
   delivering route's landing point, or, for a first appearance with neither, from the point farthest inside the
   shape. The front is eased: slow first cell, accelerates, settles, arrives.
 - LOST cells recede in the same window, farthest from the remaining shape first, unless another polity's spread
   over that ground has begun by then, in which case they go exactly when that front arrives (taken, not emptied).
 - A polity that ends recedes after its last year, over half its last span, farthest from its core first.
 - Where the source draws two polities on one cell at one time, the cell holds both and is drawn striped.

attribution.changes_made: Changes were made. Features filtered to those overlapping this act window; polygons simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 0.25 degrees (topology preserved), invalid geometries repaired, and coordinates snapped to a 0.01 degree grid (2 decimal places); properties reduced to Name (n), FromYear (f), ToYear (t) and Wikidata Q-ID (w).

changes_made_here: Changes were made: this act's polygons (simplified at 0.25 degrees when the acts were cut) were rasterised to 0.1-degree cells; composite records are not drawn; the growth and retreat between two dated shapes is computed by this map (method above) and is not in the source.
